messages.subject: Which omega for BIG-5 personality scale?
parts:
Dear Lavaan-group!

We want to calculate the realibility for a second-order CFA model.
In semTools::compRelSEM(), should we use ord.scale=T when analyzing a CFA model based on 5-point likert scale questionnarie data (estimator="WLSMV", ordered=T)?

What could be the reason that some omega coefficients are bigger than 1? (model converged without warnings)

###BACKGROUND

Where "A_... " are individual items, e.g. A_08037 is "I act reserved towards strangers."
"letter.number" are facets, e.g. E.5 is "risk-taking",
and letters are domensions, e.g. E = "extraversion", ES = "emotional stability"...

Items are rated on a 5-point likert scale, therefore, we use WLSMV estimation for our CFA models, e.g. fit.BIG5 <- lavaan::cfa(cfa.BIG5, data = dat, estimator="WLSMV", ordered=T)

Finally, to calculate reliability, we want to use compRelSEM(fit.BIG5, higher = c("E", "ES", "O", "G", "V"), tau.eq=F, ord.scale=T) - will that yield the correct omega coefficient? Or should we specify something in "config=..."?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Which omega for BIG-5 personality scale?
parts: should we use ord.scale=T when analyzing a CFA model based on 5-point likert scale questionnarie data (estimator="WLSMV", ordered=T)?

That is what Green & Yang (2009) recommended.   I agree that the variance of a composite is determined by its observed ordinal-scale values (1 through 5), but I am not so confident about G&Y's trick to define the proportion of that (observed-scale) variance that is attributable to the common factor, based on parameters that are on the latent-response scale.  When we calculate a composite of observed items, we are not adding up the latent responses; we are adding up the observed responses.  At the very least, I would recommend additionally treating the data as continuous and reporting that omega.
What could be the reason that some omega coefficients are bigger than 1?

Not sure.  I only tested the higher-order feature on a model with a single higher-order factor.  Make sure you use the most recent semTools on GitHub, in case this is a bug I already fixed:

https://github.com/simsem/semTools/wiki
we want to use compRelSEM(fit.BIG5, higher = c("E", "ES", "O", "G", "V"), tau.eq=F, ord.scale=T) - will that yield the correct omega coefficient?
That is what would give you the omega defined by Green & Yang (2009).
should we specify something in "config=..."?

No, that is for MLSEM, to specify within-level constructs when cases are nested in clusters.
